question: Where can I get flood hazard zones (geometry) in Spain, with return period or probability and the issuing authority?

answer.summary: MITECO's SNCZI WFS (gis.miteco.gob.es/geoserver/agua/wfs) serves flood-zone polygons for T=10, 50, 100, 500 years for all 25 demarcaciones, with promoting authority (organismo) per feature, CC BY 4.0. Coverage is studied river reaches only (about 22-36% of main rivers), fluvial only. Producers (CHE, CHC, CHT, CHG, IDEIB, ACA, La Palma) add newer or extra layers. Coastal T100/T500 exists only as raster (WMS).
main_caveats: Absence of a polygon is not absence of hazard: SNCZI covers only studied reaches (T100: 33,3 % of main rivers; T500: 36,2 %).
Bulk shapefile downloads on gis.miteco.gob.es sit behind an altcha captcha; the WFS (CC BY 4.0) is the scriptable route. Full q500 is huge (200 features = 65 MB).

organismo is the promoter of the study, not necessarily the current issuer; spellings vary and dates can be empty. Producer services (CHT shapefiles, ACA WFS) lack an authority field; cycles 1 to 3 coexist (field ciclo).
Coastal T100 is described as 'probabilidad baja' by IDEE coverages, while Directive scenarios call T100 medium; treat the label with care.
Layer bbox property is lat,lon while GeoJSON geometry is lon,lat; WFS layer is EPSG:4258.
answer.confidence_reason: Main WFS and 12 producer endpoints tested with counts; 14 units only PDF/viewer, blocked or unreachable from this machine; coastal vector not found after several sites.

how_to_use.example_request: curl -s -G 'https://gis.miteco.gob.es/geoserver/agua/wfs?service=WFS&version=2.0.0' --data-urlencode 'request=GetFeature' --data-urlencode 'typeNames=agua:Zi_laminas_q100' --data-urlencode 'bbox=39.3,-0.5,39.6,-0.2,urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::4326' --data-urlencode 'count=1' --data-urlencode 'propertyName=id_zona,organismo,demarcacio,ciclo,fecha_apro,zona' --data-urlencode 'outputFormat=application/json'  (same without propertyName gives geometry; add resultType=hits for counts)
how_to_use.example_result: {"features":[{"id":"Zi_laminas_q100.247","geometry":null,"properties":{"id_zona":"ES080_T100_112","zona":"40.41 BARRANC DE PEDRALVILLA - 40.42 BARRANCO DE OLOCAU O DEL CARRAIXET","fecha_apro":"2011-10-31T23:00:00Z","organismo":"Ministerio de Agrigultura, Alimentación y Medio Ambiente","demarcacio":"Júcar","ciclo":1}}],"numberMatched":12}. Without propertyName: MultiPolygon, tipo_zona "Q Periodo de retorno T100", hipotesis "Q100 régimen alterado", estudio "SNCZI. Zonas Inundables del Sistema Júcar II".
steps: Pick the layer by return period: Zi_laminas_q10 (6086 features), q50 (3455), q100 (6256), q500 (6246); also ZI_Laminas_ZFP (5978, preferential flow zone) and Zi_arpsi (3094 line segments, not polygons).
Use resultType=hits for counts; filter with bbox or cql_filter (e.g. demarcacio='Segura' gave 599 T100 zones; ciclo=3 gave 156).
Request outputFormat=application/json; geometry is MultiPolygon in EPSG:4258 as lon,lat; use propertyName to avoid heavy geometry.
Read the authority from organismo and the basin from demarcacio; the scenario is the layer plus tipo_zona/hipotesis.
Merge layers by stacking them and keeping the T from the layer name.
reading_traps: Heavy: count=200 on Zi_laminas_q500 returned 65 MB and 3.7 million vertices; page with count/startIndex and filters.
The bbox in each feature properties is lat,lon order (35.269,-2.9541) while geometry coordinates are lon,lat.
organismo has spelling variants and old ministry names (e.g. "Agrigultura"); in a 1000-feature T100 sample ordered by id, 555 were Agència Catalana de l'Aigua, 12 Generalitat Valenciana.
1968 of 6256 T100 zones have ciclo -9999 (not a Directive ARPSI zone); zi_directiva NO means pre-Directive study.
fecha_apro is blank for some features (e.g. a Melilla cycle-3 file in the basin zip) and q_m3_s is text with comma decimals and semicolons.
Bulk zip links (DescargaFichero?f=laminasPB-q500.zip) return an HTML page with an altcha captcha widget, not the file; WFS is the scriptable route.
0 of 3,714,801 vertices in a 200-feature q500 sample fell outside Spain bounds (lon -19..5, lat 27..44.5).

National T100 counts per demarcación (6256 total): Tajo 972, Cataluña 709, Duero 694, Segura 599, Miño-Sil 598, Cantábrico Occ. 547, Ebro 411, Júcar 375, Cantábrico Or. 358, Guadalquivir 315, Galicia Costa 282, Mediterráneas Andaluzas 167, Guadiana 112, TOP 37, Guadalete-Barbate 32, Tenerife 8, Fuerteventura 7, Gran Canaria 6, Lanzarote 6, Melilla 5, Ceuta 5, Baleares 4, La Palma 3, La Gomera 3, El Hierro 1; cycle 3 only in 7 of them (Ebro 99, Miño-Sil 19, Duero 10, Segura 10, Tajo 9, Guadalquivir 6, Melilla 3).

First Ebro record: ID_ZONA ES091_T100_AAR_04a08, TIPO_ZONA "Q Periodo de retorno T100", HIPOTESIS "Q100 régimen alterado", ESTUDIO "SNCZI de la Demarcación Hidrográfica del Ebro. ARPSI Alto Arga". steps: Find the producer page in the member list; services are ArcGIS REST (CHE, CHC, IDEIB, La Palma), WFS (ACA) or zips (CHT, CHG).
For ArcGIS REST, list services with ?f=json, query layers with where=1=1 and returnCountOnly=true, then outFields=*&resultRecordCount=2.
For zips, download with GET (CHT returns 500 to HEAD), unzip with python3 -I zipfile and read dbf/prj.
Check each layer for an authority field: CHE, CHC, CHG, Baleares have ORGANISMO; CHT hazard dbf and ACA WFS do not.
Deduplicate against the national WFS by id_zona (ES091_... Ebro, ES018_... Cantábrico) because the national set already contains the same zones.
reading_traps: File names mix DHG (Guadalquivir) and DHM (Melilla) prefixes; DHM_* is Melilla, not Guadalquivir.
The shp.xml metadata still points to an internal network path (source Q100_2Ciclo_PB_20241121_ETRS89), so it is an extract of the national layer.
In the dbf the dates FECHA_APRO may be empty and numeric fields are stored as floats (CICLO 3.0e+00).
ArcGIS layers return dates as epoch milliseconds, and -2209161600000 (1900-01-01) appears as FECHA_APRO placeholder in Baleares.
ACA geometries are EPSG:25831 (UTM), CHT zips are ETRS89 UTM 29/30, CHE/CHC/CHG are geographic; check prj or spatialReference.
CHT hazard shapefiles have one polygon named T100 per ARPSI and no authority/date fields; the zip name is the ARPSI code.
Same zones appear in several sources: Ebro 411 and Cantábrico Occidental 547 equal the national counts, so summing sources double counts.
